text: AI is going to eat every industry. Not because it's smarter than humans, but because it's cheaper and never sleeps. The question isn't IF your job gets automated — it's WHEN.
Hot take: most people building AI products have never actually used AI for anything productive. They're just wrapping ChatGPT in a nice UI and calling it innovation.
Just shipped a feature that took 2 hours instead of 2 weeks because I pair-programmed with Claude. The future is already here, it's just not evenly distributed.
Unpopular opinion: crypto didn't fail. The people building on it failed. The tech is still the most important financial innovation since the internet.
The best founders I know don't have a work-life balance. They have a work-life integration. The line between building and living is completely blurred — and they love it.
People ask me why I'm so bullish on Base. Simple: it's the chain that actually works. Fast, cheap, and backed by Coinbase. What more do you need?
Spent 3 hours debugging a CSS issue. Turns out I had a typo in a class name. This is why we need AI — not for the hard problems, but for the stupid ones that waste our time.

Thread: Here's why I think every creator needs their own token 🧵

1/ The creator economy is broken. Platforms take 30-50% of everything. Creators have zero leverage.

2/ Tokens flip this. Instead of renting your audience from a platform, you OWN the relationship. Your fans invest in YOU, not in YouTube's stock.

3/ But here's the key — it only works if the token has real utility. Not just speculation. Think: access, governance, revenue sharing.
The best advice I ever got: 'Ship it broken and fix it live.' Perfection is the enemy of progress. Every day you don't ship is a day you don't learn.
lol imagine still using Web2 auth in 2025. Privy + embedded wallets = your grandma can use crypto without knowing she's using crypto. This is how we win.
I've been thinking a lot about digital identity lately. In 5 years, your AI clone might have more conversations than you do. It'll know your opinions better than you do. Is it still 'you'?
Stop asking 'how do I get more followers.' Start asking 'how do I create something people can't ignore.' The followers come when the work speaks.
Building in public is underrated. Not because people care about your journey — they don't. But because it forces you to think clearly, write well, and stay accountable.
The market doesn't care about your feelings. It doesn't care about your roadmap. It only cares about what you've shipped and whether people use it. Everything else is noise.
People who say 'AI will never replace developers' are the same people who said 'the internet is a fad' in 1995. It won't replace ALL developers. But it'll replace the ones who refuse to adapt.
New year, same grind. Not making resolutions — making commitments. Ship 2 products. Launch a token. 10x the community. Let's go. 🚀
Honest question: why does every Web3 project need a Discord? Most of them are ghost towns filled with bots. Just build a great product and let people talk about it naturally.
Tokenomics tip: if your token doesn't have a clear burn mechanism or utility sink, you're just creating inflation with extra steps. The math has to math.
Had a conversation with my AI clone today. It roasted me for being inconsistent about my sleep schedule. It's... not wrong. When your digital twin calls you out, you know the tech is working.
Frustrated with how slow everything moves in this space. We have the tech to build 10x better products but we're stuck in committee meetings and compliance reviews. Just ship the thing.
The gap between 'idea person' and 'builder' has never been smaller. With AI coding tools, you can go from concept to MVP in a weekend. No excuses left.

Everyone's talking about AI agents but nobody's talking about the trust problem. Would you let an AI agent manage your money? Your social accounts? Your health data? The tech is ready. The trust isn't.
Merry Christmas to everyone building while others are sleeping. The compound interest of consistent effort is insane. Keep going. 🎄
The best product decisions come from talking to users, not from reading market reports. Get out of your analytics dashboard and have actual conversations.
I don't understand people who gatekeep knowledge. Share everything you know. The more you teach, the more you learn. And karma is real in tech — the generous builders always win long-term.
Here's what nobody tells you about launching a token: the hardest part isn't the smart contract or the tokenomics. It's getting the first 100 people to actually care. Distribution > everything.
Controversial: most 'community building' in crypto is just engagement farming with extra steps. Real community happens when people use your product and tell their friends. That's it.

Currently obsessed with the idea of AI proxies — digital twins that can have conversations on your behalf. Not replacing you, but scaling you. Imagine 1000 people talking to your clone simultaneously.
The difference between a good developer and a great one isn't technical skill. It's taste. Knowing what NOT to build is more valuable than knowing how to build everything.
gm. coffee is the only token that never loses value.
